author: Joey Peters
title: Here's a list of everyone who has been convicted in the Feeding Our Future case
notes: A running tracker of Feeding Our Future guilty pleas and trial convictions, explicitly modeled on Sahan Journal's own defendant tracker ('As Sahan Journal tracks the growing number of defendants in the case, we'll also track...'). States 70 charged and 37 pleaded guilty as of this March 21, 2025 snapshot. Most per-defendant entries give no exact plea date (two early entries -- Bekam Merdassa and Hadith Yusuf Ahmed -- give 'October 13' and Abdul Abubakar Ali gives 'October 26', all without a stated year in the retrieved text); dollar amounts and case detail are otherwise specific and consistent with this corpus's existing sourcing for the same defendants (e.g. Jama/Brava family, Zamzam Jama restitution, Sharon Ross sentence range). Retrieved via direct fetch with a browser user-agent after an initial WebFetch attempt returned HTTP 403.
supports: As of March 21, 2025, 70 people had been charged and 37 had pleaded guilty in the Feeding Our Future investigation.

Abdulkadir Nur Salah, 38, co-owner of Safari Restaurant, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; Safari was alleged to have received $16 million in fraudulent funds; he agreed to pay $5.5 million in restitution and a recommended sentence of 9 to 11.5 years.

Abdi Nur Salah, 37, a former aide to Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; he registered Stigma Free International, admitted pocketing more than $1 million in fraudulent federal funds, and agreed to a recommended sentence of roughly two years.

Abdikadir Ainanshe Mohamud ('AK'), 33, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; he ran the Stigma-Free Willmar food site at FaaFan Restaurant, admitted siphoning more than $5 million, and agreed to a recommended sentence of roughly four to five years.

Qamar Hassan, 54, of Brooklyn Park, pleaded guilty to money laundering and conspiracy to commit wire fraud; she owned and operated S&S Catering and admitted transferring more than $800,000 of S&S Catering's proceeds to her own bank account for personal purchases including a Jeep Wrangler, a Range Rover, a Brooklyn Park townhome, and an apartment in Nairobi, Kenya.

Filsan Hassan, 29, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering; she operated Youth for Higher Educational Achievement, which claimed to serve more than 1 million meals between April and December 2021 and received more than $2.5 million in federal food-aid dollars; she admitted spending $114,000 of that money on a Brooklyn Park townhome jointly with co-defendant Qamar Hassan, and agreed to pay $361,000 in restitution.

Abdul Abubakar Ali, 40, co-ran the Youth Inventors Lab food site and pleaded guilty on October 26 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting the site never served a single meal despite claiming 1.3 million meals to obtain $3 million in federal food-aid money.

Haji Salad, 34, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; he ran Haji's Kitchen, which purported to supply more than 17 million meals; he admitted stealing $19 million and pocketing $11.4 million, and agreed to pay $11.4 million in restitution with a recommended sentence of roughly five to six-and-a-half years.

Anab Awad, 53, headed the nonprofit Multiple Community Services (five food sites in Minneapolis, Osseo, and Faribault) and pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud for fraudulently obtaining $9.3 million; she claimed 3.8 million meals served but admitted in court to serving only a fraction of that number.

Sharmarke Issa, 43, ran Minnesota's Somali Community, which operated food sites claiming to serve 2.3 million children; he pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud, agreed to pay $3.6 million in restitution, and had separately served nearly three years as board chair of the Minneapolis Public Housing Authority (MPHA), the first Somali in the nation to chair a public housing agency governing body.

Farhiya Mohamud, 65, pleaded guilty to one count of money laundering; her plea deal states she was not involved in or aware of the broader scheme but should have known money she received was 'criminally derived'; she admitted her son, co-defendant Sharmarke Issa, directed her to buy real estate using money from co-defendants Haji Salad and Fahad Nur; prosecutors and her defense recommended a one-year probationary sentence.

Liban Yasin Alishire, 42, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and one count of money laundering; he claimed 870,000 meals served through Community Enhancement Services and Lake Street Kitchen, fraudulently obtaining $2.4 million and keeping $714,000; he agreed to pay $714,000 in restitution and forfeit a Kenyan resort, a Kenyan apartment unit, a Ford F150, and a boat and trailer.

Kawsar Jama, 42, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; she operated four food sites including one in Pelican Rapids that claimed to serve 2,560 children daily (exceeding the city's total population of 2,500); she agreed to a recommended prison term of about three to three-and-a-half years and to pay just over $1.3 million in restitution.

Abdikadir Kadiye, 51, pleaded guilty to wire fraud; he used Hobyo Health Care Foundation to register three meal sites in Eden Prairie, Minneapolis, and Minnetonka, stealing more than $1 million by submitting a roster of invented children's names; he agreed to pay $876,897 in restitution; no sentencing date had been set as of this article.

Abdulkadir Awale, 50, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; he enrolled three restaurants he owned in the federal program over a 21-month period, stealing more than $11 million spent on his home mortgage, two semi trucks, and a Chevy Traverse SUV, and agreed to pay more than $2 million in restitution.

Khadra Abdi, 42, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; she ran the Shafi'i Tutoring & Homework Help Center food site and fraudulently claimed close to $3.5 million in reimbursements between April 2020 and December 2021; she and prosecutors agreed to a recommended sentence of 2.25 to 2.75 years.

Ayan Farah Abukar, 43, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud; she founded Action for East African People, received about $5.7 million in federal funds, paid more than $330,000 in kickbacks to a Feeding Our Future employee, and spent money on a commercial property in Lakeville and an aircraft in Kenya.

Mohamed Ali Hussein, 53, of Faribault, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; his nonprofit Somali American Faribault Education claimed to serve 2,500 meals a day; together with co-defendant Lul Bashir Ali he admitted defrauding the government of more than $5 million, and both agreed to repay that amount and forfeit three properties and one car.

Lul Bashir Ali, 57, of Faribault, pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud; she claimed to feed 1,600 children a day through her restaurant, Lido Restaurant, and admitted inflating numbers via fake attendance records and invoices; with co-defendant Mohamed Ali Hussein she agreed to repay more than $5 million and forfeit three properties and a car.

Mulata Ali, 38, of Minneapolis, pleaded guilty to one count of aiding and abetting the theft of public money; he operated Franklyn Transportation LLC, alleged to have been used to launder more than $2 million, and was paid close to $100,000 for use of the business's bank account; his plea agreement calls for a guideline sentence of 24 to 30 months and $95,099 in restitution.

Bekam Merdassa, 40, co-ran Youth Inventors Lab and pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting the shell company never served a meal but collected $3 million by claiming 1.3 million meals served between December 2020 and June 2021.

Hadith Yusuf Ahmed, 33, previously monitored Feeding Our Future food sites and pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting he accepted $1 million in kickbacks from food sites and started a shell company, Southwest Metro Youth, that received $1.1 million by falsely claiming to feed 2,000 children a day.

Hanna Marekegn, 40, owned Brava Cafe, a Minneapolis restaurant, and pleaded guilty on October 13 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, admitting Brava Cafe received $7.1 million by claiming to serve more than two million meals between September 2020 and January 2022, and that she gave more than $150,000 in bribes to Feeding Our Future employees.
does_not_support: This is journalism aggregating a running tracker, not the primary plea agreements, judgments, or charging instruments themselves; no primary court record for any of the 22 defendants listed above has been independently retrieved by this corpus as of this pass.

Exact plea dates for the great majority of entries listed here; only three entries (Bekam Merdassa, Hadith Yusuf Ahmed: 'October 13'; Abdul Abubakar Ali: 'October 26') give even a partial date, and none of the three states a year in the retrieved text.

Any sentencing outcome for the 22 defendants listed above; all described sentence/restitution figures are plea-agreement recommendations or admissions, not judgments -- Abdikadir Kadiye's entry explicitly states no sentencing date had been set as of publication.

'Brava Cafe' (Hanna Marekegn's Minneapolis restaurant, referenced here) should not be confused with 'Brava Restaurant & Cafe LLC' (the separate Rochester restaurant tied to the Sharmake/Ayan/Zamzam/Mustafa/Asha/Fartun Jama family in case 22-CR-225); these appear to be two distinct businesses despite the similar name.

This corpus's docket assignment for 'Yusuf Bashir Ali' (fof-d-030, grouped under 22-CR-224); this article's separate 'Yusuf Ali, 41' (tied to Youth Inventors Lab, which is not one of this corpus's docketed case groups) is not confirmed to be the same person and is not used to update fof-d-030 in this pass.
